headline: Van Gerwen survives De Graaf as Humphries and Wade go through
standfirst: Michael van Gerwen needed a deciding leg to beat Jeffrey de Graaf 5-4 after missing ten match darts, and the group stage closed with the last-16 line-up set.
body: Michael van Gerwen scraped into the last 16 of the Grand Slam of Darts on Tuesday night, beating Jeffrey de Graaf 5-4 in Wolverhampton despite failing to convert ten match darts. Luke Humphries and James Wade also secured their places as the final group matches were played.

Van Gerwen led 3-1, only for De Graaf to win two legs in a row and square the match at 3-3. The Swede then missed a chance to move in front at 4-3, and Van Gerwen responded with a 25 checkout to move within a leg of victory. He could not take any of his match darts, which allowed De Graaf to level at 4-4, but the Dutchman settled the decider on double eight. He now plays Wade in the last 16.

Wade made sure of his own progress by whitewashing Ricky Evans 5-0. Humphries beat Joe Cullen 5-2 and goes on to meet Tom Sykes, who had earlier beaten Krzysztof Ratajski 5-1 to come through his group.

Gian van Veen was level with Bradley Brooks at 2-2 before winning two successive legs and then closing out a 5-2 victory on double eight. He faces Martin Schindler, who beat Chris Dobey 5-3 to finish top of their group.

Nathan Aspinall ended his group campaign with a 5-0 win over Karel Sedlacek, according to Dartsnews, with an average above 100 and a 97 checkout. He plays Gabriel Clemens, who beat Rusty-Jake Rodriguez 5-3 in his final group match.

Four Dutch players are now in the knockout stage: Van Gerwen, Van Veen, Jermaine Wattimena and Kevin Doets. The last-16 ties so far are Van Gerwen v Wade, Humphries v Sykes, Van Veen v Schindler and Aspinall v Clemens.
